name: IDTrue
tip: Search your name with the form on this page and select the record that is you. Then tap the link they email you to confirm. It is free and takes effect at once. One email address can remove up to 3 records. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Information.com
tip: People search with its own Suppression Center. Enter your email, tick the box and tap Continue. Then tap the link they email you and follow its steps to remove your records. Most requests take effect in 5 to 7 days.

name: PeopleWhiz
tip: Search your name on this page and follow the prompts to remove your record. They ask for proof of identity before they finish. They email you when the removal starts and say it takes up to 5 business days. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Archives.com (owned by Ancestry)
tip: Sells searches of records about living people. Fill in your name and address, choose Same as above for the requester, give your email twice and put a short request in the Additional Information box. Tick the box to agree, do the CAPTCHA and submit. They say about 30 days and email you when it is done.

name: Ancestry (records of living people)
tip: Its paid search includes address and phone records of living people. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST, send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. Ancestry says it decides removals from its record indexes case by case, and it may ask for ID to confirm who you are.

name: IDI (idiCORE lookup database)
tip: Runs idiCORE, a people-lookup database sold to businesses. This deletion form is open to Texas residents. Fill in your name, address, mobile number, email and date of birth, answer the two questions, choose where to send the confirmation, set today's date, tick the box, do the robot check and tap Submit Request.

name: Swordfish AI (cell numbers and emails)
tip: Sells people's cell numbers and email addresses to recruiters and sales teams. Fill in your first name, last name and email, add your phone number so they can find it, and tap Remove. They say within 30 days and email you when it is done.

name: Nymeria (emails and phone numbers)
tip: Contact finder that sells people's emails and phone numbers. Fill in your name, email and phone, choose Do Not Sell as the request and tap Submit.

name: Wiza (contacts taken from LinkedIn)
tip: Builds contact lists from LinkedIn profiles. If you have never had a LinkedIn profile, tap NOT LISTED. Otherwise enter your full name and email, add your LinkedIn link if you have it, and submit. They say up to 30 days. Their public directory has its own removal form on the same site.

name: FaceCheck.ID (face search)
tip: Anyone can upload a face here and get matching photos from around the web. To be removed, search with a photo of yourself, tap Remove My Photos, pick the photos that are you and prove it with a selfie. It is free and the photos are hidden right away. This means giving them a photo of your face, so tap NOT LISTED to skip it if you would rather not.

name: PimEyes (face search)
tip: A face search engine open to anyone. Its opt-out form asks for a clear photo of your face, a scan of your ID with the sensitive details covered, and your email. They then keep your face out of their results. Tap NOT LISTED to skip it if you would rather not send those.

name: Unified ID 2.0 (ad tracking by email and phone)
tip: An advertising ID that ad companies build from your email address or phone number. Enter your email, tap NEXT and follow the prompts. Then do it again with your phone number, because each one is opted out separately.

name: Yahoo ConnectID (ad tracking by email and phone)
tip: Yahoo's advertising ID, built from your email address and phone number. Enter your email and cell number and tap Submit. Then tap the link they send you to finish.

name: AtData (email address data)
tip: Sells data tied to email addresses to marketers. Fill in your email, name and address, tick the robot check and submit. Do it once for each email address you use.

name: Infutor (identity data)
tip: Identity data company. Its opt-out is open to anyone in the US. On its privacy rights form choose the opt-out request, fill in your details and submit, then follow any email they send.

name: Throtle (identity data)
tip: Matches emails, home addresses and phone numbers to people for advertisers. Texas residents can use this form to opt out and delete. Give your name, every email address you use, your home address and your phone number, then submit. They say 15 days for an opt-out and 45 for deletion. Or call 866-672-5235.

name: Semcasting (identity data)
tip: Identity data company for advertisers. Its Privacy Choice opt-out is free for anyone in the US. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST, send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. The email carries your home address if it is saved under EDIT MY DETAILS. They record it within 10 to 30 days. Or call 888-401-0387.

name: Claritas (marketing data)
tip: Sorts households into marketing groups and sells the lists. They need your first and last name and home address to act. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the email gives all three if your street address is saved under EDIT MY DETAILS. Send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. They say 45 days. Or call 888-994-9312.

name: Adstra (marketing data)
tip: Runs marketing data for direct mail and online ads. Anyone in the US can use this form to stop them passing your details on for marketing and to ask for deletion. Fill in your details and submit. They may ask for a notarized statement to confirm who you are, and say they pay for it.

name: L2 (voter and consumer data)
tip: Data company behind many voter and consumer lists. They take deletion requests by email and ask for your full name and address. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the email gives both if your street address is saved under EDIT MY DETAILS. Send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. If you move or change your name, send it again.

name: TargetSmart (voter and consumer data)
tip: Data company for political campaigns. On this page tap TargetSmart Consumer Privacy Webform and give your full name, home address and email. They do not take requests by email, and they may mail you a letter with a step to finish. Or call 888-678-6880.

name: i360 (voter and consumer data)
tip: Data company for political campaigns and a data broker under Texas law. On its form choose the delete and do-not-sell requests, fill in your details and submit, then follow any email they send.

name: Valpak (coupon mailers)
tip: The blue envelope of coupons. Fill in your name, mailing address, phone and email, tick the box and tap Submit. Mailings can take several weeks to stop.
